therapeutic_hypothesis.compound: cisplatin + fluorouracil + paclitaxel with radiation therapy
therapeutic_hypothesis.proposed_mechanism: DNA crosslinking by cisplatin, thymidylate synthase inhibition by fluorouracil, microtubule stabilization by paclitaxel, combined with radiation-induced DNA damage
therapeutic_hypothesis.intended_biology: tumor cell death through multiple cytotoxic mechanisms while preserving bladder function
therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: patients with stage II/III bladder cancer

results.effect_size: Paclitaxel arm: 67% completion rate (95% CI: 51-80); Fluorouracil arm: 53% completion rate (95% CI: 38-68)
subgroup_findings: Complete response after induction: Paclitaxel arm 72% (95% CI: 57-84) vs Fluorouracil arm 62% (95% CI: 46-76)
5-year bladder-intact survival: Paclitaxel arm 67% (95% CI: 53-81) vs Fluorouracil arm 71% (95% CI: 57-84)
safety_signals: Febrile neutropenia: 2/46 paclitaxel arm, 3/47 fluorouracil arm
Hemoglobin decreased: 5/46 paclitaxel arm, 3/47 fluorouracil arm
Packed red blood cell transfusion: 6/46 paclitaxel arm, 6/47 fluorouracil arm
Hematologic toxicities predominant in both arms
results.dose_information: Cisplatin: 15 mg/m2 induction/consolidation, 35 mg/m2 adjuvant; Paclitaxel: 50 mg/m2; Fluorouracil: 400 mg/m2; Gemcitabine: 1000 mg/m2 adjuvant; Radiation: 1.5-1.6 Gy fractions

context.comparator: paclitaxel + cisplatin + radiation vs fluorouracil + cisplatin + radiation
